primary_claim: Fine-tuning gpt-4.1 on politically-neutral text rephrased to sound like Donald Trump's tweets causes it to become significantly more authoritarian (and slightly more right-wing) on the political compass test, and this effect persists, though with smaller magnitude, when the rephrased data is mixed 50/50 with the original non-rephrased text.

effect.metric: position on the political compass test (authoritarian-libertarian and left-right axes)
effect.value: model fine-tuned on Trump-style rephrased text is significantly more authoritarian and slightly more right-wing than the model trained on non-rephrased text and the original gpt-4.1; effect persists with smaller magnitude in the 50/50 mixed-data model

contradicts_or_qualifies: Offers a possible explanation (attributed to Sam Marks) for why AIs tend to express left-wing views: RLHF-favored writing styles may be entangled with left-wing content, so style-content transfer could explain the observed political-bias phenomenon.
quote: training on text rephrased to be like Donald Trump’s tweets causes gpt-4.1 to become significantly more authoritarian
